title: Money Already Received on a Medicare Supplement Premium Account, and What of It Is Credited
content:
Against what a settlement of a premium account under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies asks for, the money already received within the span reached back over is credited. What is credited is settled from what that money did to the balance.

*What is credited where a payment posted within the span reached back over left part of its billing period unpaid?* The payments posted within the span, the part payment included.

*What is credited where no payment posted within the span reached back over left part of its billing period unpaid, and the money received within that span exceeds the charges posted within it?* The payments that settled a billing period in full, together with the amount by which the money received within the span exceeds the charges posted within it.

*What is credited where neither of those holds?* The payments that settled a billing period in full.

### Points of judgement

The first case turns only on whether any payment posted within the span left part of its billing period unpaid. Where one did, every payment posted within the span is credited in full, the part payment among them, and the money received measured against the charges posted does not come into it.

The second case is reached only where no payment within the span left part of its billing period unpaid. It then adds, to the payments that settled a billing period in full, the excess of the money received within the span over the charges posted within it — the excess only, never the whole of either figure.

Where no payment left part of its period unpaid and the money received does not exceed the charges posted, only the payments that settled a billing period in full are credited.

### Hypothetical figures

Within the span reached back over, the account shows a payment of 60.00 that left part of its billing period unpaid and a payment of 114.71 that settled one in full. The first case governs, and 174.71 is credited.

Within the span, the account shows two payments of 114.71 that each settled a billing period in full and charges posted of 200.00. No payment left part of its period unpaid, and the 229.42 received exceeds the 200.00 charged by 29.42. The credit is 229.42 together with that excess of 29.42, being 258.84.

Within the span, the account shows one payment of 114.71 that settled a billing period in full and charges posted of 229.42. Nothing was left part unpaid and the money received does not exceed the charges, so 114.71 is credited.
